article_content: Apple's iOS 7.1.1 update has caused technical issues for some users, with reports of devices becoming unresponsive or entering recovery mode. While primarily affecting Over-The-Air (OTA) updates, some installations via iTunes also encountered problems. The update, intended to enhance battery life and security, impacted devices including iPhone 4S, 5, 5C, 5S, iPad Air, iPad mini, and iPod Touch. Multiple users on Apple's forums described needing full restores after update failures, resulting in data loss. Brandtley reported: 'My device got stuck in recovery mode post-update.' While termed 'bricked' by some, most devices remained recoverable through system resets. The 26MB update specifically resolved a TouchID fingerprint recognition issue on iPhone 5S and improved keyboard responsiveness on older models. Apple advises users to backup data via iCloud/iTunes and ensure sufficient storage before updating. Detailed instructions for both OTA and iTunes update methods are available on Apple's support page, with warnings about potential installation challenges.

Kuigi värskenduse eesmärgiks oli parandada aku eluiga ja turvalisust, tekkisid eriti õhu kaudu (OTA) installimisel tõrked, osadel juhtudel ka iTunesi kasutamisel. article_content: Paris, France (CNN) -- A strike by air traffic controllers disrupted flights across France on Wednesday, leading to the cancellation of 10% of scheduled flights at Paris' main Charles de Gaulle Airport, according to the civil aviation authority DGAC. Half of all flights from Orly Airport, France's second-largest air hub, were also canceled. Authorities advised passengers to confirm flight statuses with airlines before traveling. Irish carrier Ryanair called on the French government to deploy military personnel for air traffic control duties during the strike, stating: 'France, passengers, and airlines cannot tolerate these disruptions during a critical period for travel and tourism.' The strike coincides with the start of summer vacations for many French residents. EasyJet passenger Nawel Boubouka, whose Orly flight was postponed to Thursday, expressed frustration: 'Finding accommodation in mid-July is extremely difficult.' The labor action, ongoing since Tuesday evening, is set to conclude Thursday at 6 a.m. Controllers are protesting Europe's air traffic control integration plans. France is preparing to join Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg in forming FABEC (Functional Airspace Block Europe Central), part of the Single European Sky initiative aimed at optimizing flight paths to reduce fuel consumption and flight times. The FABEC zone spans 1,713,442 square kilometers and contains Europe's busiest civil and military air routes.

Pool Orly lennujaama lendudest, mis on riigi suuruselt teine lennujaam, tühistati samuti. Reisijaid paluti lennu olekut kontrollida enne lennujaama saabumist. Iiri odavlennufirma Ryanair nõudis Prantsusmaa valitsuselt sõjaväe kaasamist õhuliikluse juhtimisse streigi ajal, öeldes: 'Prantsusmaa, reisijad ja lennufirmad ei saa selliseid häireid taluda reisi- ja turismihooaja tipus.' Streik langeb kokku paljude prantslaste suvepuhkuste algusega. EasyJeti reisija Nawel Boubouka, kelle Orly lend lükati üle neljapäevaks, väljendas meelehärmi: 'Majutuse leidmine juuli keskpaigas on ääretult raske.' Tööseisukord, mis kestis teisipäeva õhtust alates, lõppeb neljapäeval kell 6 hommikul. Kontrollörid protestivad Euroopa õhuliikluse ühendamise plaanide vastu. Prantsusmaa valmistub liituma Saksamaa, Šveitsi, Belgia, Hollandi ja Luksemburgiga FABEC-i (Funktsionaalne õhuruumiplokk Kesk-Euroopa) moodustamiseks, mis kuulub Ühtse Euroopa taeva programmi hulka. Selle eesmärk on lennutrajektoore optimeerida, et vähendada kütusekulu ja lennuaegu. FABEC-i tsoon hõlmab 1 713 442 ruutkilomeetrit ning sisaldab Euroopa kõige tihedamaid tsiviil- ja sõjalennuliine.

article_content: Celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay emphasizes cooking as an essential life skill, advising his children to prioritize it over exam results. He recently told his 15-year-old son Jack to focus on kitchen skills rather than stressing about a Latin exam, stating culinary literacy better addresses childhood obesity than academic pressure. Despite leaving school with minimal qualifications and a curtailed football career, Ramsay built a multi-million pound culinary empire. 'The obesity crisis stems from parents' poor nutritional knowledge, not kids,' he declared on the David Letterman show. 'I told Jack: If Latin won't be part of your life, let's perfect scrambled eggs instead.' Ramsay's four children now prepare weekend family meals, showcasing skills he helped develop. He attributes his values to mother Helen Cosgrove, who worked at Stratford-upon-Avon's Cobweb Tea Room: 'She brought home unsold food—we never wasted anything. Modern kids often lack basic kitchen responsibilities.' On Masterchef Junior, Ramsay observes children as young as eight outperforming adults: 'They learn faster and handle feedback constructively. These skills build real confidence—I critique parents, not kids.' His daughter Matilda, 13, will host CBBC's 'Matilda and the Ramsay Bunch,' combining Bollywood-themed cooking with adventure challenges. Born in Scotland in 1966, Ramsay overcame a difficult childhood before pursuing catering. After a football injury ended his sports aspirations, he studied at North Oxford Technical College, eventually earning Michelin stars and TV fame through shows like Kitchen Nightmares and Hell's Kitchen.

article_content: Archaeologists have uncovered an unusual Iron Age burial in Wiltshire suggesting ancient fears of restless spirits. A female skeleton missing her feet was discovered alongside animal remains and other human burials during infrastructure work by Wessex Water. The burial site near West Knoyle revealed a woman interred with severed feet placed beside her, along with sheep and goat remains positioned near her head. Adjacent graves contained a 10-year-old child and two men with sword-related injuries. Dr. Melanie Giles from the University of Manchester notes this reflects preventive funerary practices. 'Post-mortem foot removal appears designed to stop spiritual unrest,' she stated. Such measures typically followed deaths considered spiritually risky, including violent fatalities or childbirth complications. Iron Age burial customs varied regionally, from corpse exposure to stone cist interments. This discovery highlights complex ritual practices, with animal offerings potentially serving as both spiritual protection and afterlife provisions.

article_content: The StartupBus competition represents a high-intensity entrepreneurial challenge. Forty teams across six buses complete a 48-hour journey from multiple U.S. cities to Austin's SXSW festival, developing business prototypes during transit. Participants, called 'buspreneurs,' operate under severe time constraints that organizers compare to crisis-response scenarios. Unlike typical SXSW startups that prepare for months, StartupBus teams conceptualize and develop during the journey. The 2011 event features a simulated stock exchange game where players invest in developing projects. Participation grew from 50 applicants in 2010 to 1,200 in 2011, with 160 selected competitors. While 2010 winners DormDorm (dorm rental concept) and DateBrowsr (dating profile aggregator) didn't become operational businesses, alumni report significant career benefits. DormDorm team member Mick Johnson later joined Y Combinator. The 2011 competition includes documentary teams and reporters from CNN, CNET, and All Things Digital.

article_content: UK authorities warn that synthetic opioids like AH-7921 - marketed as Doxylam - pose unprecedented risks, with Home Office Minister Norman Baker calling them more dangerous than traditional narcotics. The death of Jason Nock, a computer technician who fatally overdosed on the legally available substance in 2013, highlights the crisis. Government data shows legal high-related fatalities in England and Wales surged from 12 in 2009 to 97 in 2012, with two-thirds directly caused by the substances. Officials struggle to control new psychoactive compounds engineered weekly to evade drug laws. Recent prison disturbances at HMP Blantyre House in Kent have been tied to synthetic cannabis 'Spice', banned in 2009 but still circulating undetected. An expert panel including toxicologists and law enforcement representatives is developing strategies to address this evolving threat, with recommendations expected by late spring.

Inglismaa ja Walesi andmetel tõusis seaduslike uimastitega seotud surmajuhtumite arv 12-lt 2009. aastal 97-ni 2012. aastal. Kenti Blantyre House'i vangla vägivallaintsidenteid seostatakse 2009. aastal keelatud sünteetilise kanepiga 'Spice', mida tavalised uimastitestid ei tuvasta. article_content: Recent reports suggest Michael Schumacher has begun recognizing immediate family members while remaining nonverbal nearly a decade after his December 29, 2013 skiing accident in Meribel's French Alps. Philippe Streiff, a former racer using a wheelchair since his 1989 crash, told media outlets the Formula 1 icon demonstrates early cognitive awareness but faces profound physical challenges. Streiff alleges receiving updates from Corinna Schumacher and neurosurgeon Gerard Saillant, claiming the seven-time champion manages minimal limb movement and practices sitting upright. These assertions conflict with official statements from manager Sabine Kehm, who stresses Schumacher's recovery remains 'a long fight' and denies Streiff's claimed connections to the family. The life-changing injury occurred when Schumacher diverged from a marked red slope (intermediate difficulty) onto ungraded terrain between red and blue runs. A partially concealed rock caused loss of control, propelling him 34 feet into another rock formation. After six months in induced coma and subsequent hospital care, Schumacher now receives treatment at his Lake Geneva residence, with therapists cautiously hopeful about potential future mobility using crutches.

Endine võidusõitja Philippe Streiff, kes kasutab ratastooli alates 1989. aasta õnnetusest, väidab meedias, et seitsmekordne F1-meister näitab esimesi märke teadvuse taastumisest, kuid seisab silmitsi tõsiste füüsiliste väljakutsetega. Osaliselt varjatud kivi põhjustas tasakaalukaotuse, tõugates teda 10 meetri kaugusele teise kivini. Pärast kuut kuud tehiskoomas viibimist ja hilisemat haiglaravi saab Schumacher nüüd ravi Genfi järve ääres asuvas kodus, kus terapeudid hoiavad ettevaatlikku lootust tema võimalikule liikumisvõimele karkude abiga.

article_content: Scotland's Justice Secretary Kenny MacAskill allegedly advised Lockerbie bomber Abdelbaset Al-Megrahi to withdraw his appeal to facilitate compassionate release, according to claims in a new book. The 2009 meeting with Libyan officials reportedly included suggestions that dropping legal challenges would expedite Megrahi's release, though Scottish authorities deny any involvement. Medical professionals had given Megrahi three months to live due to prostate cancer, but he survived 2.5 years post-release, intensifying scrutiny of the decision. The book 'Megrahi: You Are My Jury' contends the conviction resulted from flawed investigations and political maneuvering, while UK officials maintain the release was unjustified. Political opponents demand parliamentary investigation into alleged secret negotiations.

Uue raamatu 'Megrahi: Teie olete mu vandekogu' kohaselt pakuti 2009. aastal Liibüa delegatsiooniga peetud kohtumisel välja, et kohtuprotsessist loobumine kiirendaks vabastamisprotsessi. article_content: Joseph Gibbons, a 61-year-old filmmaker and former MIT lecturer (2002-2010), faces robbery charges for allegedly stealing $1,000 from a Manhattan Capital One bank on December 31st while documenting the act as artistic research. According to court filings, Gibbons presented a note requesting church donations during the incident. Rhode Island authorities connect him to a similar November 2023 Citizens Bank robbery in Providence where $3,000 was taken. Fellow detainee Kaylan Sherrard reported Gibbons described the robberies as film research during their custody, stating: 'It's not a crime; it's artwork.' Historical records show Gibbons previously told Big Red and Shiny magazine he engaged in drug-related activities as 'romantic artistic research' for short films. MIT's archived webpage confirms Gibbons' lecturing tenure and international exhibitions at institutions including MoMA and Centre Pompidou. His 2002 film 'Confessions of a Sociopath' was listed among Artforum's annual best films. Multiple attempts to reach Gibbons for comment were unsuccessful.

Kohtumaterjalide kohaselt esitas Gibbons pangatöötajale kirjaliku nõude annetuseks oma kirikule. Rhode Islandi ametivõimud seovad teda sarnase 2023. aasta novembris toimunud 3000 dollari suuruse röövimisega Providence'is asuvast Citizens Bankist. Tema 2002. aasta film 'Sotsiopaadi ülestunnistused' valiti kunstiajakirja Artforum aasta parimate filmide hulka. Kommenteerimispalved Gibbonsile jäid vastuseta.

article_content: When Rachel Frederickson, 24, appeared at NBC's 'The Biggest Loser' finale, her dramatic transformation sparked concern. The voice-over artist from Los Angeles lost 59.62% of her body weight, dropping from 260 pounds to 105 pounds. At 5'5", her BMI of 17.5 falls below the NIH's underweight threshold of 18.5. While trainers Bob Harper and Jillian Michaels declined to comment, social media reactions ranged from alarm to disappointment, with some users describing her as 'frail' and urging her to seek help. Medical experts emphasized that while BMI has limitations, extreme weight loss carries risks. Dr. Steven Lamm of NYU's Preston Robert Tisch Center for Men's Health noted severe weight reduction can cause hormonal issues and bone density loss. Northwestern Comprehensive Center on Obesity's Dr. Robert Kushner stated most patients lose 30% body weight annually, adding that swinging between weight extremes resembles 'a pendulum.' Both experts stressed that modest weight loss can significantly improve health markers like cholesterol and blood sugar.

article_content: This November 2nd, video game enthusiasts can support pediatric healthcare by participating in a unique fundraising marathon. Through initiatives like Extra Life, now part of Children's Miracle Network Hospitals, players commit to extended gaming sessions while collecting donations - with this year's challenge extended to 25 hours due to daylight saving time adjustments. The concept originated in 2007 when founder Jeromy Adams sought game donations for Tori Enmon, a young cancer patient. The overwhelming response revealed gamers' charitable potential, leading to Extra Life's creation following Tori's passing in 2008. Adams emphasizes that modern gamers often balance family responsibilities while maintaining their passion: 'We're connected, efficient communicators wanting to make meaningful contributions.' Parallel initiatives like Humble Bundle demonstrate similar philanthropy. Their pay-what-you-want model (first introduced in 2010), allowing buyers to allocate portions to charities, surpassed expectations by raising $1.2 million initially versus $200,000 projections. Default 20% charity allocations often increase through user choice, benefiting organizations like Electronic Frontier Foundation and American Red Cross.

Üleujuv vastus viis Extra Life'i loomiseni 2008. aastal pärast Tori surma. article_content: A Maryland mother accused of stabbing her two youngest children during an attempted exorcism led an informal religious group called 'Demon Assassins,' according to court documents. One-year-old Norell Harris and two-year-old Zyana Harris were found deceased in their Germantown home on January 17, 2014. Their mother Zakieya Avery (28) and family acquaintance Monifa Sanford (21) face murder charges for the children's deaths and attempted murder charges for attacks on the victims' older siblings. Prosecutors stated Avery had planned an exorcism ritual for a friend the day before the killings, though he didn't attend. The women later told police they believed the children were possessed, describing darkened eyes and a black cloud during the attack. Court records indicate Avery attempted to break her son's neck before stabbing both younger children, then injured the older siblings aged 5 and 8. Authorities revealed Avery had previous mental health commitments, while Sanford reported prior suicide attempts. Both women claimed their 'Demon Assassins' group, formed through Germantown's Exousia Ministries church, previously conducted non-violent spiritual practices. Church leadership stated the suspects hadn't been active members at the time of the incident. Surviving children were hospitalized in stable condition. Family members expressed shock, with the victims' grandmother describing them as 'the sweetest things.' Both suspects remain held without bond pending trial.

article_content: Authorities have obtained surveillance footage of an individual who made a 911 call reporting an armed man heading toward Yale University on November 26, 2013. The call, received at 9:48 AM from a payphone one mile from campus, triggered a six-hour lockdown and multi-agency response involving SWAT teams and federal agents. New Haven Police Chief Dean Esserman described the caller as 'a confused gentleman' whose account became less credible throughout the day. Initial witness reports of a gunman were later attributed to police officers carrying rifles during early response efforts. Yale officials confirmed no threat was found after thorough campus searches. With classes canceled for Thanksgiving week, normal operations were scheduled to resume December 2. Police are interviewing multiple persons of interest, indicating the incident may have been a prank. Students expressed relief after the lockdown ended, with freshman Samantha Brown stating: 'It feels safe now and I'm glad it's over.'

article_content: Redlands College Principal Mark Bensley has drawn criticism after refusing two final-year Muslim teaching students wearing hijabs from beginning their placement at the Queensland Christian school. The decision sparked widespread social media backlash, with parents and community members questioning its compatibility with Christian values of acceptance. Parent Jennie Duke expressed disappointment, stating she was 'so very sad' her daughter attends the institution. Online commentators rebranded the school 'Redneck College,' while others challenged the religious justification: 'It's not very Christian-like to reject teachers over hijabs,' one critic wrote. Bensley defended his actions in the school newsletter, citing his 'duty of care to ensure staff support Christian principles.' He acknowledged the women's right to wear hijabs but claimed the practice conflicted with school values, arranging their transfer to another institution. The college's official statement emphasized commitment to Christian education while denying wrongdoing: 'We believe all parties reached mutual agreement.' They maintained the decision reflected educational alignment rather than intolerance. Religious leaders from multiple faiths condemned the move. Reverend Anneli Sinnko (identified as female) called it 'a contradiction of Christian foundations,' while Islamic representatives expressed deep concern. Legal experts noted Queensland's Anti-Discrimination Act permits religious requirements for school staff, complicating potential challenges.

article_content: October 2023 marked historic weather extremes in County Armagh, breaking two major records according to Armagh Observatory's 185-year dataset. The month saw 195.4mm of rainfall, surpassing the 1870 record of 193.8mm. Concurrently, temperatures reached 21.7°C - the third-highest October reading ever recorded at the facility and the warmest single day in 97 years. Severe flooding impacted multiple counties including Armagh, Down, and Antrim, with County Down experiencing its wettest October on record. Professor Michael Burton, the observatory's director, emphasized these patterns reflect climate change: 'Extreme weather is becoming routine rather than exceptional. Warmer air holds more moisture, leading to both increased rainfall and temperature extremes.' The observatory's continuous meteorological records since 1838 provide robust evidence of shifting climate patterns. Professor Burton noted that while individual events shouldn't be overinterpreted, the long-term data clearly shows increasing challenges for climate adaptation and the urgent need for mitigation efforts.

Samal ajal tõusid temperatuurid 21,7°C-ni – see on kolmas kõrgeim oktoobritemperatuur observatooriumi ajaloos ja kuumim päev viimase 97 aasta jooksul. Rängad üleujutused tabasid mitmeid Ulsteri krahvkondi, sealhulgas Downi krahvkonda, mis koges oma märgemat oktoobrit alates mõõtmiste algusest. Armagh'i Observatooriumi direktor professor Michael Burton selgitas: 'Äärmuslikud ilmastikunähtused muutuvad tavapäraseks. article_content: Brazilian Formula 1 driver Felipe Massa has raised urgent safety concerns about Pirelli's selected tires for November's home Grand Prix, the season's penultimate race. The veteran racer labeled the decision to bring only medium and hard compound tires to Interlagos as 'extremely risky,' citing unpredictable weather and recent track renovations. Massa emphasized the circuit's anti-clockwise layout places unique stress on tires, worsened by potential rain and colder temperatures. 'Choosing these compounds makes no sense and puts drivers at unnecessary risk,' he stated during the Russian GP weekend. The Williams driver noted he'd consulted extensively with colleagues and officials but remained unsatisfied with Pirelli's rationale, with safety concerns heightened by Jules Bianchi's 2014 crash in Japan. Pirelli's motorsport director Paul Hembery responded that harder tires had proven effective in previous Interlagos races, preventing the blistering issues seen with softer compounds. While acknowledging the resurfaced track surface might require reevaluation, he emphasized any changes would depend on technical data analysis before the tire working group's next meeting.

article_content: In a 2010 New York attack, gunman William Spengler killed two firefighters using weapons illegally obtained through Dawn Nguyen's straw purchase. Federal authorities report Nguyen, then 24, falsely claimed ownership of an AR-15 rifle and 12-gauge shotgun during their June 7, 2010 acquisition. Spengler, who had served 17 years for murdering his grandmother in 1980, died by suicide after the ambush. Recovered firearms included two .223-caliber Bushmaster rifles - the same model used in the 2012 Sandy Hook shooting - and a Mossberg shotgun. Nguyen faces federal charges with potential penalties of 10 years imprisonment and $250,000 fines.

article_content: Paramount Australia has apologized after unintentionally referencing 9/11 in promotional materials for 'Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles'. We're deeply sorry and have discontinued its use.' The film, starring Megan Fox and Johnny Knoxville, releases in August in the US and October in Europe. Australia's September 11 date coincides with the 13th anniversary of the attacks that killed 2,996 people, including 11 Australians. Social media reactions included criticism of the marketing choice, with users describing the timing as insensitive. Paramount deleted the original post and shared alternative promotional content. The incident highlights sensitivities around using historical trauma in commercial contexts.

article_content: Passengers have the right to be informed about denied boarding, which occurs when an airline refuses to carry a passenger who arrived on time. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) issued a show-cause notice to Air India for failing to comply with regulations on passenger facilities during denied boarding, cancellations, or delays. Airlines may overbook flights but must first seek volunteers before denying boarding. Involuntarily denied passengers are entitled to compensation, alternate flights, and assistance (meals/accommodation). Compensation amounts depend on alternative flight timing: 200% of basic fare + fuel charge (max Rs 10,000) if rebooked within 24 hours, or 400% (max Rs 20,000) if declining the alternative. Full ticket refunds are mandatory. In 2023, DGCA fined Air India Rs 10 lakh for compensation failures. For cancellations within two weeks to 24 hours before departure, airlines must provide alternatives within two hours or refunds. Compensation of Rs 5,000-10,000 applies unless caused by force majeure. To claim compensation: 1) Document all communications and tickets; 2) Contact the airline for immediate resolution; 3) File a DGCA complaint if unresolved; 4) Seek legal help if necessary.

Tsiviillennuamet (DGCA) on esitanud Air Indiale 'show cause' teate, kuna ettevõte ei ole täitnud reisijatele kehtivaid nõudeid loatauditamise, lennu tühistamise või viivituse korral. Lennufirmadel on õigus lende üle broneerida, kuid nad peavad esmalt otsima vabatahtlikke, kes loobuvad kohast. Kui vabatahtlikke ei leidu, peab lennufirma pakkuma loatauditatud reisijatele hüvitist, asenduslendu ning toitlustust ja majutust vastavalt olukorrale. Hüviste suurus sõltub asenduslennu ajast: kui pakutakse lennu, mis väljub kuni 24 tunni jooksul algselt plaanitud ajast, on hüvitis 200% põhihinnast pluss kütusekulu (maksimaalselt 10 000 INR). Kui reisija loobub asenduslennust, on hüvitis 400% (maksimaalselt 20 000 INR) ning täielik pileti tagasimakse. 2023. aastal määras DGCA Air Indiale 10 lakh INR trahvi reisijatele hüvitiste mittemaksmise eest. Lennu tühistamisel peab lennufirma pakkuma asenduslendu kahe tunni jooksul või tagastama pileti hinna. Kui lennu tühistatakse kuni kaks nädalat enne väljumist, on reisijal õigus hüvitisele 5000–10 000 INR, sõltuvalt lennu kestusest. Ülemjõuolukorras hüvitist ei maksta. Hüvitise nõudmiseks järgige neid samme: 1) Dokumenteerige kõik lennufirmaga suhtlused, pardakaardid ja intsidenti puudutavad dokumendid; 2) Teavitage lennufirmat ja nõutage hüvitist DGCA reeglite kohaselt; 3) Esitage vormiline kaebus lennufirmale ja DGCA-le, lisades kõik asjakohased dokumendid; 4) Vajadusel pöörduge tarbijakaitseorganisatsiooni või juristi poole.

article_content: Lindsay Newell, founder of an animal sanctuary established in memory of her murdered grandparents, received a conditional discharge from Burton-upon-Trent Magistrates' Court despite being convicted of six animal cruelty charges. The 27-year-old veterinary nurse's Burton Wildlife and Animal Rescue Centre in Etwall, Derbyshire, housed multiple malnourished animals during a November 2012 RSPCA inspection, including Babe the pig who died during the raid. While cleared of 25 additional charges, Newell received a five-year ban on keeping specific animals and must contribute £2,000 toward the £20,000 prosecution costs. District Judge David Taylor acknowledged Newell's overextended efforts caused unintended harm, stating: 'These were not deliberate acts but consequences of trying to do too much.'

article_content: In today's data-driven landscape, data science competitions have become a powerful tool for solving real-world challenges. Organizations increasingly use these contests to crowdsource solutions while strategically identifying potential talent. Groundbreaking research from the University of Waterloo reveals that motivating participants through optimized contest structures and incentives is crucial for success. Dr. Keehyung Kim, a professor of emerging technologies at the School of Accounting and Finance, has conducted pioneering research on motivation factors in data science competitions. "Our study analyzes common competition designs and explores how organizers can maximize contestant engagement," Kim states. "We specifically investigate whether single-stage or two-stage structures yield better results." Published in Production and Operations Management on September 8, 2023, the study titled "Designing contests for data science competitions: Number of stages and the prize structures" applies behavioral economics principles to competition design. Kim's research demonstrates that participants exert significantly more effort in two-stage competitions compared to single-stage formats. "Our behavioral model reveals the psychological drivers behind these results," Kim explains. "The fear of early elimination in two-stage contests makes the distinction between winning and losing more pronounced, motivating higher first-stage effort." The study also found that allocating most prize money to the final winner in two-stage contests increases motivation, while prize distribution has minimal impact in single-stage formats. These findings provide practical guidance for competition organizers: Implementing multi-stage structures and emphasizing progression between stages can significantly boost participation quality. Public result announcements and strategic prize allocation emerge as key non-financial motivators alongside monetary rewards.

article_content: Prosecutor Khan cannot single-handedly stop the violence but retains crucial responsibilities. The international community continues to witness mass atrocities against civilians in Palestine and Israel. These devastating events demand responses focused on justice rather than escalating violence. The International Criminal Court (ICC) remains the sole independent institution capable of investigating such international crimes. The ICC holds jurisdiction over Gaza and crimes committed by Palestinian factions including Hamas. In 2021, the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) initiated an official Palestine investigation following its determination that 'war crimes have been committed by both Palestinian and Israeli actors.' Investigative priorities include deliberate civilian targeting, hostage-taking, and indiscriminate bombings. Israel's potential collective punishment tactics against Palestinians - prohibited under the Geneva Conventions - also require scrutiny. A UN commission continues gathering evidence of recent atrocities, stating there is 'clear evidence of potential war crimes.' Human Rights Watch documents mutual violations, warning such crimes persist when accountability is neglected. While the OTP confirmed its ongoing investigation and jurisdiction over current conflicts, Prosecutor Khan's public silence remains concerning. Though the ICC cannot independently halt violence, Prosecutor Khan should unequivocally condemn atrocities and utilize available mechanisms. Since 2021, Khan has minimized symbolic actions despite their demonstrated value. His 2022 Ukraine statements - while not preventing Russian aggression - demonstrated solidarity with victims. Similar gestures for Palestine could affirm the ICC's relevance and support for human rights. Khan's apparent prioritization of 'winnable' cases creates inconsistencies, as shown by pursuing Putin despite low arrest prospects while deprioritizing Afghanistan investigations. Western opposition to Palestine probes might influence this calculus, but victims deserve equal consideration regardless of politics. Maintaining silence risks rendering the ICC irrelevant precisely when needed most. To Prosecutor Khan: Your voice and actions carry weight. Historical atrocities demand consistent application of justice principles. The court's credibility depends on demonstrating impartial commitment to human rights protections worldwide.

Tema 2022. aasta avaldused Ukraina kohta - kuigi ei peatänud Vene agressiooni - näitasid solidaarsust ohvritega. Sarnased avaldused Palestiina kohta kinnistaksid ICC asjakohasust ja inimõiguste kaitsmist. Khani näiline eelistamine 'võidetavatele' juhtumitele loob vasturääkivust, nagu näitab Putini vahistamismääruse väljastamine hoolimata madalatest võimalustest, samal ajal kui Afganistani uurimised jäeti tahaplaanile. Lääne vastuseis Palestiina uurimistele võib mõjutada seda kaalutlust, kuid ohvrid vääravad võrdset käsitlust hoolimata poliitikast. Vaikimine ohustab ICC asjakohasust just olukorras, kus seda kõige rohkem vajatakse. Prokurör Khan: Teie hääl ja tegevus on tähtsad. Ajaloolised julmused nõuavad õiguspõhimõtete järjekindlat rakendamist. Kohtu usaldusväärsus sõltub erapooletu pühendumise näitamisest inimõiguste kaitsele üle maailma.

article_content: A dental healthcare worker stands accused of contaminating her supervisor's beverage with mercury following workplace disagreements, according to court proceedings. The alleged incident occurred at Shams Moopen Dental Practice in Bedfordshire, where 35-year-old Ravinder Kaur reportedly added mercury capsules - commonly used in dental procedures - to Laura Knowles' coffee. Medical staff witnessed Knowles discovering metallic particles at the mug's bottom after tasting the drink, prompting her to discard it and seek emergency care for abdominal discomfort. While experiencing temporary symptoms, she sustained no permanent health damage. Records indicate Kaur had received formal reprimands prior to the incident, including disciplinary action for leaving a patient unattended during her lunch break. Prosecutors allege the mercury contamination occurred two months after Kaur participated in an employment tribunal, noting her professional familiarity with mercury's hazardous properties. The accused denies charges of intentionally administering harmful substances. Legal proceedings remain ongoing.

article_content: Israel's Mossad intelligence agency has declassified archival materials revealing new details about the 1960 capture of Nazi war criminal Adolf Eichmann in Argentina. The 'Operation Finale' exhibition discloses previously classified operational tactics, including forensic identification through ear analysis and the use of forged documents. Eichmann, architect of the Holocaust's 'Final Solution' that systematically exterminated six million European Jews, was captured through coordinated surveillance and extraction techniques. The exhibit features operational artifacts including concealed cameras, forged passports, and medical tools used during the capture. Curator Avner A (pseudonym) notes this operation significantly enhanced Mossad's global intelligence capabilities, requiring innovative tactics later adopted by security agencies worldwide. Eichmann's landmark 1961 trial featured unprecedented Holocaust survivor testimony before his 1962 execution - remaining Israel's only judicial death sentence.

'Operatsioon Finale' näitus paljastab seni saladuses hoitud meetodeid, sealhulgas kõrvaanatoomia alusel tehtud tuvastamist ja võltsdokumentide kasutamist. article_content: Turkey's government faced significant political upheaval this week as three cabinet ministers resigned following corruption investigations. The sons of Economy Minister Zafer Caglayan, Interior Minister Muammer Guler, and Urbanization Minister Erdogan Bayraktar were detained (with Bayraktar's son later released) in a probe into alleged money laundering, gold smuggling, and bribery. Bayraktar notably called for Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdogan's resignation during his departure, claiming political pressure. The investigation follows a two-year inquiry by Istanbul prosecutors. Concurrently, tensions escalated between Erdogan and Islamic cleric Fethullah Gulen, whose supporters allegedly hold key positions in Turkey's police and judiciary. Erdogan accused Gulen's Hizmet Movement of creating a 'parallel state' within government structures. Former Interior Minister Idris Naim Sahin also resigned from Erdogan's AKP party. In response to the crisis, Erdogan replaced 10 cabinet members while restricting press access to police stations. Scores of senior police officers were dismissed, with authorities claiming operational overreach in the corruption arrests. Journalists reported unprecedented media restrictions during the upheaval.

article_content: Manchester's Chetham Library offers a remarkable journey through time, preserving its 17th-century atmosphere where Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels first collaborated on revolutionary ideas. Established in 1653 through textile merchant Humphrey Chetham's legacy as Britain's oldest public reference library, this cultural landmark houses over 100,000 historical volumes, including rare manuscripts and peculiar artifacts. Visitors can explore original architectural features like exposed wooden beams in what was once medieval Manchester's second-largest building, discovering curiosities ranging from occult practitioner John Dee's personal items to early editions of Milton's Paradise Lost. Despite its central location near modern attractions, the library maintains a tranquil medieval ambiance while continually expanding its collections with contemporary additions like Northern Soul memorabilia.

article_content: School records reveal John Lennon's rebellious behavior as a teenager at Quarry Bank High School in Liverpool. Recently discovered detention sheets from 1955-1956, now up for auction, document multiple infractions including three detentions in one day for "fighting," "silliness," and "chewing." The documents, authenticated by Lennon's childhood friend Pete Shotton, were rescued from destruction in the late 1970s when a staff member recognized their significance during a storage room cleanup. Teachers described the future Beatles star as a "class clown" who nevertheless showed potential, with chemistry teacher Eric Oldman remarking: "John could actually go far." The auction, running from November 22 to December 1, 2013, includes other notable Beatles memorabilia such as a signed White Album estimated at £60,000-£80,000. Lennon himself later reflected: "Parents instinctively recognized I was a troublemaker."

Dokumendid, mida autentisertis Lennoni lapsepõlvesõber Pete Shotton, pääsesid hävimiselt 1970. aastate lõpus, kui koolitöötaja märkas nende ajaloolist tähtsust laopuhastusel. article_content: A four-year-old hippopotamus named Solly tragically passed away during initial rescue efforts after being trapped for three days in an 8-foot (2.4m) deep swimming pool at Monate Conservation Lodge near Johannesburg. The young animal had been forced out of its herd following his mother's recent childbirth, leading dominant males to drive him away. Lodge staff discovered Solly stranded in the steep-sided pool which lacked proper exit points. Despite draining most of the water and preparing sedation procedures, the hippo succumbed just as veterinarians arrived - with South Africa's Eyewitness News reporting the veterinary team arrived nearly four hours late. Wildlife experts used a crane to remove the one-ton animal's body from the contaminated water, which had become polluted during the prolonged entrapment. NSPCA representative Isabel Wentzel noted the hippo would've required relocation to another sanctuary due to herd rejection. The incident highlights challenges in wildlife management, particularly regarding human-made environmental hazards.

Noor loom sunniti karjast lahkuma pärast emase hiljutist poegimist, mis pani domineerivad isased ta eemale tõrjuma. Kaitseala töötavad leidsid Solly kinnijäänuna järsukülgedega basseini, millest puudusid turvalised väljapääsud. Kuigi suurem osa veest pumpati välja ja ette valmistati rahustamist, suri loom veterinaaride saabumise hetkel - Lõuna-Aafrika meediaväljaanne Eyewitness News teatas, et loomale määratud veterinaarid jõudsid kohale ligi nelja tunni hilinemisega. article_content: The landmark conviction of Liberia's former leader Charles Taylor after a six-year trial represents both progress and paradox in global justice efforts. While celebrating this unprecedented prosecution of a head-of-state for war crimes, observers question whether lengthy international trials truly serve affected communities. Taylor faced 11 charges at the Sierra Leone tribunal, including using child soldiers - a focus amplified by recent campaigns like Kony 2012. However, the case exposed systemic issues: marathon proceedings slowed by legal complexities and procedural delays, narrowly framed charges omitting Liberian atrocities, and physical/cultural distance from victims. Critics highlight three key flaws: 1) Excessive duration increasing costs while reducing impact 2) Charge selection favoring provability over representativeness 3) Court locations divorced from crime scenes. The Hague-based trial prevented Sierra Leoneans from witnessing proceedings firsthand, while foreign legal traditions created cultural barriers. As international tribunals prepare to close, Rwanda's domestic prosecution of genocide suspects offers an alternative model. Experts argue investing in local justice systems may prove more sustainable and meaningful for post-conflict societies than expensive international processes dominated by foreign legal professionals.
translated_content: Liberia endise liidri Charles Taylori ajalooline mõistmine kuueaastase kohtuprotsessi järel näitab rahvusvahelise õiguse edasiminekut ja paradokse. Kuigi selle ekspresidendi sõjakuritegude eest kohtusse toomist peetakse läbimurdeks, tekib küsimus, kas pikad rahvusvahelised protsessid tõesti teenivad kannatanute huve. Taylorile esitati Sierra Leone eritribunalis 11 süüdistust, sealhulgas lapsessõdurite kasutamine - teema, mida tõi esiplaanile Kony 2012 kampaania. Protsess aga paljastas süsteemseid probleeme: venivad menetlused õiguslike keerukuste tõttu, kitsad süüdistused, mis ignoreerisid Liberias toime pandud kuritegusid, ning füüsiline ja kultuuriline eraldatus ohvritest. Kriitikud osutavad kolmele peamisele nõrkusele: 1) Liiga pikad protsessid suurendavad kulusid ja vähendavad mõju 2) Süüdistused keskenduvad lihtsasti tõestatavatele, mitte olulisematele kuritegudele 3) Kohtuasutused asuvad kuritegude toimumispaigast eemal. Haagis toimunud protsess takistas Sierra Leone elanikel kohal viibimist, samal ajal võõrad kohtutavad komistavad kohalikku konteksti. article_content: Commuters in North Carolina got more than they bargained for this week when a highway signage error turned into an impromptu spelling test. Construction crews working on Interstate-77's southbound exit 28 ramp in Cornelius mistakenly painted 'noly' instead of 'only' - a glaring typo that now sits permanently beside its correctly spelled version. Cornelius project lead Tyler Beardsley told WBTV that contractors racing against the clock likely caused the oversight, finishing what should've been a 32-hour bridge renovation in just 18 hours. 'Speed sometimes comes at the cost of accuracy,' Beardsley admitted, confirming that crews would redo the work Monday night without using taxpayer funds. Though transportation officials remained unavailable for additional comment, the viral error has ignited discussions about infrastructure oversight. Locals continue sharing photos of the botched signage online, transforming a simple typo into a statewide conversation about construction quality standards.

'He's a gorgeous, progressive horse,' Geraghty notes, though soft ground hindered his mount Triolo D'Alene. Faugheen leads Champion Hurdle odds, but Geraghty cautions against overrating him due to untested competition. More Of That's loss is attributed to track conditions, not diminished ability. article_content: Former U.S. intelligence analyst Edward Snowden has accused the National Security Agency of routinely sharing raw, unredacted communications of Americans with Israel, according to intelligence expert James Bamford. Writing in the New York Times, Bamford reported that intercepted data included communications from Arab- and Palestinian-Americans, potentially exposing their relatives in Israel and Palestinian territories to targeting. Snowden described this as 'one of the biggest abuses we've seen,' according to Bamford. A leaked memorandum of understanding between NSA and its Israeli counterpart, first reported by The Guardian, outlines data transfers occurring since 2009. The shared material reportedly includes unevaluated transcripts, voice data, and digital metadata without removal of personal identifiers. Unit 8200, Israel's signals intelligence unit, allegedly used collected data - including sensitive personal information about Palestinians' private lives - for political coercion. Former unit members recently accused the agency of misusing intelligence to persecute Palestinians, as reported in a letter to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Snowden, currently residing in Russia under asylum protection, faces U.S. espionage charges for leaking classified NSA documents. Bamford, author of multiple books on NSA operations, conducted interviews with Snowden in Moscow for Wired magazine.

article_content: Newcastle United faces mounting pressure as discontent grows among supporters towards owner Mike Ashley and manager Alan Pardew. Despite securing a top-10 Premier League position, the club's second-half season struggles have sparked protests, including a symbolic 69th-minute walkout during their recent 3-0 victory over Cardiff City - referencing the club's last trophy win in 1969. The tension contrasts sharply with Ashley's Sports Direct business success, highlighted by this week's corporate event at St James' Park featuring celebrity appearances and staff incentives. Player controversies and lack of recent signings - with no major acquisitions since January 2013 - continue to undermine performance. The club has conceded 57 goals this season, among the league's worst defensive records. Pardew acknowledged tactical shortcomings, stating: 'I've made some calls this year where I could have been more positive.' With key players like Yohan Cabaye departing for Paris Saint-Germain in January 2014 and several signings exceeding £10m now sidelined, fans question the club's ambition despite Sports Direct's share price rising from £1.60 to £7.70 under Ashley's ownership.

article_content: A New Zealand fishing crew made a grim discovery Thursday while trawling 90 kilometers northeast of Auckland, retrieving aircraft wreckage containing human remains near Great Barrier Island. Authorities identified the debris as a 5.7-meter aerobatic biplane assembled from a kit by missing pilot Daroish Kraidy. The 18.5-meter San Kawhai vessel, operated by Sanford Limited, recovered the wreckage during routine operations. Police transferred the remains to their patrol boat for analysis in Auckland, where experts will conduct victim identification Friday. Kraidy, 53, vanished on March 25 after departing Ardmore Airfield. His fabric-covered Acro Sport plane disappeared from radar minutes post-takeoff. New Zealand's Civil Aviation Authority confirms this as the nation's only missing aircraft. Family members revealed Kraidy's history of depression, suggesting intentional disappearance. They noted its occurrence 17 days after MH370's disappearance, though no direct connection exists. The wreckage was transferred to authorities following proper maritime protocols.

article_content: In the coastal town of Taiji, Japan, a centuries-old practice continues to spark international controversy. While Westerners often associate dolphins with marine parks and family entertainment, local fishermen maintain a tradition of hunting these marine mammals for food - a custom dating back over 400 years. With approximately 3,000 residents, this community faces growing scrutiny from global activists like Ric O'Barry, a former 'Flipper' trainer turned vocal critic. Taiji locals acknowledge their dietary choices clash with foreign sensibilities but emphasize cultural continuity. 'We've consumed dolphin meat for generations,' explains retired educator Kayoko Tanaka, describing her preferred cooking methods. 'It feels unjust to face criticism for sustaining our heritage.' The conflict intensifies as activists document hunting practices. O'Barry, using disguises to avoid detection, films fishermen's methods he describes as 'barbaric,' claiming dolphins endure prolonged suffering. Meanwhile, Japanese officials like Fisheries Agency representative Joji Morishita defend regional autonomy: 'We respect diverse cultural values, just as we wouldn't question other nations' food traditions.' Health concerns add complexity to the debate. A 2005 government study revealed bottlenose dolphin meat contains mercury levels 12 times higher than bluefin tuna. Some locals like Councilman Junichiro Yamashita have pushed for dietary changes after personal tests showed mercury concentrations sevenfold above U.S. safety limits. Despite these risks, fish dealer Masaru Matsushita maintains: 'Activists overlook our cultural context while focusing solely on animal appeal.' Parallel tensions emerge in international whaling disputes, with Australia deploying monitoring ships and considering legal action against Japan's annual hunt of up to 1,000 whales. As global pressures mount, Taiji's fishermen limit media access, aware their practices face increasing opposition. O'Barry counters cultural defense arguments: 'Historical tradition doesn't justify harmful practices - we evolved from many outdated customs.'
translated_content: Jaapani rannikulinnas Taijis kestab sajandeid vanune traditsioon, mis põhjustab rahvusvahelist vastuolu. Kuigi läänemaailm seostab delfiine peamiselt mereparkidega, jätkavad kohalikud kalurid nende jahtimist toiduks - kommet, mis on püsinud üle 400 aasta. Umbes 3000 elanikuga linnakese kogukond seisab silmitsi globaalsete aktivistide nagu Ric O'Barry, endise 'Flipperi' treeneri, järjest suureneva surve all. Taiji elanikud teadvustavad, et nende toiduvalikud põrkuvad välismaalaste tunnetega, kuid rõhutavad põlvest-põlve päritud komme. 'Delfiiniliha on olnud meie toidulaual generatsioonide vältel,' selgitab pensionil õpetaja Kayoko Tanaka oma retseptide kohta. 'Kriitika meie traditsioonide säilitamise eest tundub ebaõiglane.' Konflikt süveneb dokumentaalfilmide salvestamisega. O'Barry, kasutades maskeeringuid tuvastamise vältimiseks, jäädvustab kalurite meetodeid, mida nimetab 'jõhkraks', väites et delfiinid kannatavad pikalt. Jaapani ametnikud nagu Kaluriameti esindaja Joji Morishita kaitsevad piirkondlikke õigusi: 'Me austame teiste kultuure, nagu ei seaks kahtluse alla teiste rahvaste toitumisharjumusi.' Terviseriskid lisavad debatile keerukust. 2005. aasta riiklik uuring tuvastas, et delfiiniliha sisaldab 12 korda rohkem elavhõbedat kui bluefin tuun. Mõned kohalikud nagu volikogu liige Junichiro Yamashita on propageerinud toitumismuutusi, kui isiklikud testid näitasid USA ohutusnormidest seitse korda kõrgemaid tasemeid. Kalakaupleja Masaru Matsushita vastab: 'Aktivistid ei mõista meie kultuuri konteksti, keskendudes vaid loomade armsusele.' Sarnased konfliktid ilmnevad vaalapidamise ümber, kus Austraalia saatis vaatluslaevu ja kaalub kohtuvaidlusi Jaapani aastase tuhande vaala püügi vastu. Surve kasvades piiravad Taiji kalurid meediatega suhtlemist. O'Barry ütleb: 'Traditsioon ei õigusta kahjulikke praktikaid - oleme hüljanud paljusid aegunud kombeid.'

article_content: Pakistani military officials reported intense overnight clashes as hundreds of suspected foreign militants launched coordinated assaults on border checkpoints along the 1,500-mile frontier. The violence spanning Saturday night into Sunday morning resulted in 40 attacker fatalities and six security personnel deaths, according to military spokesperson Gen. Athar Abbas. The skirmishes occurred in Mohmand district's tribal regions, a volatile area along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border where militant activity remains prevalent. Abbas described the assault as 'among the most significant border incursions witnessed,' noting attackers employed heavy weaponry including rocket systems and automatic firearms before being pushed back. article_content: A couple who met on the day World War II began and vowed never to be separated passed away within days of each other after 72 years of marriage. Aquilla Brant, 100, died just 12 days after his 96-year-old wife Catherine, fulfilling their lifelong pact. The pair, both battling pneumonia, will be cremated together. Their daughter Sue Brant, 68, shared that her parents maintained a promise to remain united in life and death. 'Dad always said he'd follow Mum within a fortnight—he passed 12 days later,' she explained. 'Though sudden, their shared passing feels like a fitting conclusion to their story.' Aquilla, whose Latin name means 'eagle,' served in the St John Ambulance during WWII. He met Catherine in 1939 while training medics at a Dalton fever hospital in West Yorkshire, where she worked as a nurse. Their romance blossomed when Aquilla sought her help acquiring tea and sugar rations. Married on April 8, 1942, at Almondbury Church, the couple honeymooned briefly in Ilkley before Aquilla joined the army. After being demobilized in 1946, he worked at a chemical plant before becoming a power station electrician, while Catherine focused on raising their three children. Reflecting on their 72nd anniversary last year, Aquilla credited their lasting union to the phrase 'Yes, dear' and mutual respect. The couple spent their final days together at Pilling House care home in Skelmanthorpe. After Catherine's sudden death from pneumonia on December 17, Aquilla was hospitalized with pneumonia and suffered a heart attack, passing peacefully on December 29 surrounded by family. Their joint funeral will occur January 8 at St John's Church, Lepton, with donations directed to the Forget Me Not Children's Hospice.
